summary: Normalization means storing each fact in one place and linking tables with keys. The school database keeps students, courses, and enrollments in separate tables so nothing is copied.
notes: In flat_schedule, moving the class means changing 5 rows. Miss one and the table says the same class meets in two rooms (an update anomaly).
Deleting the last 2 Personal Finance rows from flat_schedule would also delete the only record of who teaches it (a delete anomaly). In courses it stays.
First normal form: one value per cell. A column like courses = 'Biology, Algebra 2' breaks it; use one enrollment row per class instead.
pitfall: Splitting tables without a shared key loses the connection between them. Each enrollment needs student_id and course_id, or you can no longer tell who is in which class.
